title: Reduce prefill latency via SKU-aware kernel consolidation and clock hysteresis
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: In mixed-SKU clusters (H100 + L40S with heterogeneous MIG partitions) we observe high 95th-tail prefill latency and jitter caused by frequent per-request kernel routing and aggressive GPU clock scaling. Small prefill batches (token-prefill for chat warm-starts) are being dispatched across multiple MIG partitions and sometimes across different SKUs which forces repeated kernel selection and driver-level clock-ups. This causes 95p prefill latency spikes, increased latency variance, and worse CPU/GPU utilization.

Goal: Reduce 95th-percentile prefill tail by consolidating prefill kernel invocations onto SKU/MIG-friendly placements and add a clock hysteresis controller to avoid rapid clock toggles during transient load spikes. Deliver measurable improvements without regressing throughput or increasing cost.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- 95th-percentile prefill latency reduced by >=25% on mixed H100/L40S testbed (baseline: 320ms => target <=240ms) for typical chat warmup workload (batch size 8-16, seq_len 128).
- Clock scaling events per minute reduced by >=80% for the same workload.
- No more than 5% regression in median throughput for sustained generation workloads.
- Canary rollout shows no increase in error rates or OOM events for 48h across dedicated pools.

Notes: This ticket focuses on runtime heuristics and controller logic; a follow-up may be required if low-level driver/kernel changes are needed.
decisions: Implement SKU-aware kernel consolidation: prefer co-locating prefill requests to the same kernel invocation when they target identical model versions and contiguous token ranges.
Add clock hysteresis controller with two thresholds: scale-up threshold (short ramp-up) and scale-down delay (hold for 10s) to avoid oscillation.

Prefer warm KV-cache partitions for prefill routing rather than lowest-latency SKU only; route to H100 for large contiguous prefills, L40S for medium ones, but avoid splitting small batches across SKUs.
Expose a config flag (runtime.kernel_consolidation=enabled) for canary and gradual rollout.
Keep a safety fallback to per-request routing in case of MIG occupancy fragmentation or driver errors.
Defer kernel-level micro-optimizations to follow-up after validation of heuristics on prefill telemetry.
perf_results: Baseline (mixed H100/L40S testbed): 95p prefill = 320ms, median = 110ms, clock-events = 12/min
Throughput: median generation throughput change measured -2.8% (within target).
Memory: no increased peak GPU memory observed on canary runs.
Observation: fragmentation in small MIG partitions (1g.1) still causes some residual tail; see tasks item for mitigation.
tasks: Finalize kernel consolidation heuristic: detect identical model version + contiguous token ranges + compatible quantization profile.
Implement clock hysteresis controller and unit tests (configurable up/down thresholds and hold time).
Add telemetry hooks: clock-event counter, kernel-coalesce counter, per-request routing tag for post-hoc analysis.
Run large-scale perf job on staging fleet (H100/L40S mixed) and produce Grafana dashboard snapshot.
Canary rollout: enable runtime.kernel_consolidation on 10% of dedicated pools for 48h, monitor 95p latency and OOMs.
If residual fragmentation high, propose fallbacks: prefer allocating contiguous MIG partitions or preempt tiny partitions for prefill batches.
Write runbook entries describing behavior and how to revert rollout flags.
Coordinate with infra for a driver micro-patch if we observe driver-level clock race conditions (see dependency ENG-114321).
